title: The event loop in 60 seconds
caption: The JavaScript event loop in 60 seconds: how one thread juggles thousands of things at once.

scenes.title: The event loop
scenes.say: The event loop, in sixty seconds.
JavaScript runs on one thread. One thing at a time. Yet it handles network calls, timers and clicks without freezing.
The trick is to never wait.

items.title: Hand off
items.say: Slow work, like a network call, is handed off.

items.title: Queue
items.say: When it finishes, its callback joins a queue.

items.title: Loop
items.say: Whenever the thread is free, the loop takes the next one.

scenes.say: That's why a zero millisecond timeout still runs last. It has to wait for the queue.
One long task freezes everything. That's the event loop.
